MM=.227185/1024

def trajectory(stroke,shift=(0,0),speed=.012,lag=1.1):
    from scipy.interpolate import PchipInterpolator
    a=np.array(stroke,float);xy=a[:,:2]*MM;rad=a[:,2]*MM
    ss=np.r_[0,np.cumsum(np.linalg.norm(np.diff(xy,axis=0),axis=1))]
    t=np.arange(0,ss[-1],speed*.05);t=np.r_[t,ss[-1]]
    f=PchipInterpolator(ss,xy,axis=0);fr=PchipInterpolator(ss,rad)
    c=f(t);tang=f.derivative()(t);tang/=np.linalg.norm(tang,axis=1)[:,None]
    width=fr(t)*2
    dep=(width+.0007)/1.15
    lead=lag*dep+.0009
    tip=c+tang*lead[:,None]
    # Target pixels -> world; optional world xy translation for practice
    world=np.c_[-.1+.227185/2-tip[:,1]+shift[0],.227185/2-tip[:,0]+shift[1],.0202-dep]
    return world

def write(stroke,shift=(0,0),label='calligraphy',lag=1.1):
    p=trajectory(stroke,shift,lag=lag)
    move(p[0,0],p[0,1],.05)
    # Enter with a moving, light tip, then develop the stroke's width.
    start=p[0].copy();start[2]=.0205
    line([[p[0,0],p[0,1],.05],start],.015,label+' approach')
    line([start,p[0]],.012,label+' enter')
    send([list(x)+Q for x in p],label)
    end=p[-1].copy();end[2]=.028
    line([p[-1],end],.025,label+' lift')
    move(end[0],end[1],.065)
